summary: Validates a write request (offset a3, size a4) against an indexed buffer managed at a2 and returns the byte pointer at which the write lands. Three checks run in sequence. First a capacity guard: if a3+a4 exceeds the buffer capacity at a2+4, or a4 exceeds the max element size at a2+12, or the element array at a2+0 is null, an error (code 20) is dispatched through the error object a1's vtable. Second a position-window check against the current write position at a2+24 and the window length at a2+16: out-of-window requests force a reposition, dispatching sub_5164A6 (flag 1) when a pending-reprocess flag at a2+33 is set, erroring (code 68) when reprocess is disallowed at a2+34, then repositioning a2+24 either to a3 or to (a3+a4 minus window) clamped to zero, and finally dispatching sub_5164A6 (flag 0). Third a written-position bound at a2+28: when a3+a4 exceeds it, the bound is extended to a3+a4 (when a5 is set, erroring with code 20 first if a3 is past the old bound), and if the zero-fill flag at a2+32 is set the gap elements are zero-filled via MemoryZeroFill with element size (a2+8)<<7. When a5 is set the pending flag at a2+33 is raised and the resulting pointer is returned; otherwise errors on out-of-bounds writes.

local_names.a1: error object whose first dword is a vtable pointer; the vtable entry at +0 takes a1 and is used to dispatch error codes (20/68) written at a1+0x14
local_names.a2: buffer manager struct: element array (+0), capacity (+4), element stride (+8), max element size (+12), window length (+16), write position (+24), written bound (+28), zero-fill flag (+32), pending-reprocess flag (+33), reprocess-allowed flag (+34)
local_names.a5: commit flag: when set, errors are tolerated, the written bound and pending flag are updated, and the write pointer is returned; when clear, out-of-bounds conditions error
local_names.v7: current write position read from a2+24
local_names.v11: zero-fill byte size: element stride (a2+8) shifted left by 7

operations.description: Compute the requested end offset v6 = a3 + a4
Capacity/validity guard: error when a3+a4 exceeds the capacity at a2+4, or a4 exceeds the max element size at a2+12, or the element array at a2+0 is null
On the capacity/validity failure, write error code 20 into the error object at a1+0x14
Dispatch the failure: call the error object's vtable entry (the first dword of a1) with a1 as argument
Position-window guard: the write is out of window when a3 is below the write position at a2+24, or v6 exceeds position plus window length at a2+16; the reposition path then runs
When reprocess is disallowed (byte at a2+34 is zero), write error code 68 into a1+0x14 and dispatch it through the error object's vtable
When the pending-reprocess flag at a2+33 is set, dispatch sub_5164A6(a2, a1, 1) and clear the flag at a2+33
Reposition the write position at a2+24: when a3 is at or below the old position it becomes v6 minus the window length at a2+16 clamped to zero; otherwise it becomes a3
Dispatch the reposition completion: sub_5164A6(a2, a1, 0)
Written-position bound guard: the extend path runs only when the bound at a2+28 is below the requested end v6

When the written bound at a2+28 is below the start a3: if a5 is set, write error code 20 into a1+0x14 and dispatch it, then adopt a3 as the new start; if a5 is set the bound at a2+28 is extended to v6
When the zero-fill flag at a2+32 is set, walk every element index in [write position, v14) and zero-fill it through MemoryZeroFill with byte size (element stride at a2+8) shifted left by 7
Per-gap-element zero-fill: MemoryZeroFill invoked with the element pointer (from a2+0 + 4*index) and the fixed fill size
On the non-zero-fill path with a5 set, raise the pending-reprocess flag at a2+33 to 1
Compute and return the write pointer: element array base at a2+0 plus 4 times (a3 minus the write position at a2+24)
When a5 is clear and the write is out of bounds at the written-position guard, write error code 20 into a1+0x14, dispatch it through the error object, and fall through to the pointer computation path
